jobs.title: Chief AI Officer
jobs.description:
Axial Search is a specialist executive search firm built for one kind of hire: leaders who help organizations navigate AI transformation. Apply today to express your interest in roles like this one.

Visit our website to learn more about our process and explore free tools for your job search, including our live job market dashboard with salary, skills and hiring trend data from thousands of AI transformation roles.

What The Market Looks Like

Chief AI Officer roles in Canada remain sparse but growing—we've tracked 9 executive-level AI strategy postings across the country over the last six months, concentrated in Ontario, Quebec, and British Columbia. Technology, financial services, and professional services firms are leading hires. Compensation for this cohort ranges from $180k to $330k annually. The strongest candidates combine deep technical fluency with board-level communication skills, proven experience scaling AI initiatives across large organizations, and the ability to translate business strategy into executable AI roadmaps.

Job Responsibilities

Own the development and execution of the organization's AI strategy, including technology roadmap, capability building, and integration across business units
Lead the assessment, evaluation, and deployment of AI tools and platforms to drive competitive advantage and operational efficiency
Build and scale high-performing teams—data scientists, ML engineers, and AI specialists—while fostering a culture of experimentation and continuous learning
Partner with C-suite and board members to translate AI opportunities into business outcomes, manage risk, and secure investment and resources
Drive cross-functional collaboration to identify use cases, pilot programs, and full-scale implementations across the enterprise
Establish governance frameworks, ethical guardrails, and compliance standards for responsible AI deployment
Represent the organization externally—engage with industry peers, vendors, and thought leaders to stay ahead of market trends

Candidate Requirements

12+ years of experience building and scaling AI, machine learning, or data science capabilities, with at least 5 years in a leadership or executive role
Proven track record taking AI initiatives from strategy through implementation and measuring business impact at scale
Strong technical foundation—hands-on knowledge of ML/AI architectures, generative AI, and modern data platforms; you don't need to code daily, but you speak the language fluently
Experience leading and recruiting technical talent, building organizational structures, and embedding AI literacy across non-technical teams
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex AI concepts to non-technical audiences and influence executive and board-level decision-making
Understanding of AI governance, ethics, risk, and compliance in regulated or risk-sensitive industries

jobs.title: Director, Systems & Data Transformation
jobs.description:
HSB Canada, part of Munich Re, is Canada’s premier engineering-driven specialty insurer—bringing deep technical expertise to help clients stay ahead of complex, emerging, and technology-based risks. We blend specialty insurance with inspection, engineering, and technology-enhanced services to redefine what risk protection can be, with leading capabilities across areas such as cyber, equipment breakdown, renewable energy, and IoT technology services.

Backed by Munich Re, one of the world’s most experienced and financially stable insurance and reinsurance groups, HSB Canada combines global strength with deep knowledge of the Canadian market. Building on a long legacy of innovation and technical excellence, we continue to evolve our capabilities to address modern and emerging risks—from cyber and artificial intelligence to connected technologies.

Primary Objectives

The Director, Systems & Data Transformation is accountable for shaping and executing HSB Canada’s enterprise systems, data, and digital transformation agenda. Acting as a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Director translates business priorities into an integrated multi-year roadmap, leads complex cross-functional programs, and delivers measurable improvements in growth, customer and broker experience, operational effectiveness, decision-making, and risk management.

The role provides strategic and operational leadership for the transformation and optimization of the Guidewire ecosystem and its surrounding applications, integrations, data platforms, and controls, ensuring reliable and scalable support for policy, billing, claims, underwriting, and insurance operations.

The Director also leads the delivery of major business-facing capabilities, including Quote, Bind and Issue (QBI), underwriting workflow, digital experiences, enterprise data products, analytics, and responsible AI solutions, in close partnership with business, technology, operations, risk, and global stakeholders.

Success requires an enterprise-minded leader who can connect strategy, architecture, data, delivery, change management, and operational execution; build high-performing multidisciplinary teams; and establish the governance, partnerships, and performance disciplines needed to sustain transformation outcomes.

Job Responsibilities

Transformation Strategy & Portfolio Delivery
Define and maintain an integrated, multi-year systems, data, and digital transformation strategy aligned with enterprise priorities and target business outcomes
Own the transformation portfolio from business case and prioritization through delivery, adoption, value realization, and transition to operations
Establish portfolio governance, roadmaps, investment plans, budgets, resource capacity, milestones, benefits, and executive reporting
Manage cross-program dependencies, delivery risks, organizational constraints, and competing priorities; escalate decisions with clear options and recommendations
Define measurable outcomes and key performance indicators, using performance insights to continuously improve delivery and business value
Core Systems Transformation & Guidewire Leadership
Set the strategy and roadmap for the specialty insurance technology ecosystem, balancing modernization, resilience, scalability, security, cost, and speed to market
Provide accountable leadership for the Guidewire platform and surrounding applications, including architecture, configuration, integrations, data flows, environments, releases, and lifecycle management
Lead major core-platform initiatives, including ClaimCenter transformation, while maintaining service continuity, production stability, support readiness, and effective control design
Digital Insurance & QBI Transformation
Lead end-to-end delivery of Quote, Bind and Issue capabilities and underwriting workflow improvements in partnership with underwriting, product, operations, distribution, and technology teams
Establish a scalable, reusable QBI architecture that supports multiple specialty products, distribution channels, evolving underwriting models, and integration with core platforms
Champion underwriter-centered design, process simplification, automation, and adoption to improve experience, quality, and cycle time
Data Science & Responsible AI
Define and mature HSB Canada’s enterprise data and data science capabilities, including data strategy, governance, quality, architecture, platforms, and reusable data products
Partner with business leaders to identify and deliver AI use cases across underwriting, claims, operations, finance, and distribution
Ensure data and AI solutions are explainable, secure, measurable, and embedded into business processes and decisions
Operating Model & People Leadership
Build, lead, coach, and retain a high-performing multidisciplinary team spanning business systems analysis, product and application leadership, data engineering, analytics, and data science
Define clear mandates, decision rights, accountabilities, delivery standards, and career pathways; create a culture of ownership, collaboration, inclusion, innovation, and continuous learning
Develop workforce and sourcing strategies that balance internal capability, global partnerships, and external expertise while managing capacity and succession risk
Advisory, Change Leadership & Influence
Serve as a trusted advisor translating complex system and data topics into clear choices, trade-offs, recommendations, and decisions
Build alignment across Canadian and global stakeholders, facilitate executive governance, and communicate progress, risks, investment needs, and realized outcomes with clarity
Lead organizational change and adoption for new capabilities, and bring external perspective, emerging practices, and market insight to continuously evolve HSB Canada’s business and technology environment

Qualifications

University-level education in computer science, business administration, risk management, or equivalent professional experience
8–12 years demonstrated experience in business, technology, or product roles; insurance or broader financial services
Structured, hypothesis-driven problem solving: ability to frame ambiguity, develop options, assess trade-offs, and drive to clear decisions.
Strong analytical capability: extracting insights from data and market research and translate them into strategy and action.
Multi-workstream leadership: proven ability to manage multiple initiatives in parallel while maintaining quality, pace, and stakeholder alignment.
Executive communication: ability to produce crisp, compelling materials and present complex topics simply and persuasively to senior audiences.
Strong P&C insurance (or broader financial services) product knowledge—coverage/wordings, underwriting appetite, pricing fundamentals, and regulatory considerations is an asset
Experience building ecosystems/partnerships (vendors, data providers, technology partners) to enable product and service innovation is an asset

Company Benefits:

Together, we engage with everything we have and are, to help humankind act braver and better. Go further with HSB.

We are pleased to offer our employees great benefits and resources to support their mental, physical and financial wellbeing. These include:

An engaging and collaborative environment that promotes continuous learning and development
A hybrid work environment that combines weekly in-office and remote days
A great compensation package including an annual company bonus
Competitive company-paid flexible health and dental benefits, starting on your first day
Flexible dollars provided by the company to put towards a Health Spending Account and/or Wellness Spending Account
Wellness program with tools and resources supporting your mental, physical, and financial wellbeing – on and off the job
Participation in the DC Pension Plan with a progressive employer contribution scale based on tenure starting at 4%, plus optional company match in the RRSP plan
Generous time off including vacation, personal days, unplanned time, Statutory Holidays and company-wide early closure half-days
Learning and development programs and resources, including unlimited access to LinkedIn Learning, Education Assistance Program, and reimbursement for professional fees
Employee Referral Program and Recognition Program

Our base salary range for this role is between $159000 to $186000 per year, plus an opportunity for an annual company bonus based upon a percentage of eligible pay. The salary estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for candidates hired in this position. Factors that may be used to determine your actual salary include your specific skills, how many years of experience you have and comparison to internal equity.

This role is located in our Toronto office on 390 Bay St, and we operate in a hybrid work model. This job posting is for an existing vacancy.

We do not use AI in our recruitment process - applications are reviewed by our team to ensure a fair and personalized experience.

HSB Canada is committed to providing a work environment that is inclusive and free of employment barriers and discrimination. Accommodations will be made for qualified applicants with a disability throughout the recruitment process. If you receive a request for an interview and you have a disability which will require an accommodation to support your participation, please consult with Human Resources or contact hr@hsb.ca as soon as practical so that suitable accommodations can be arranged.

We thank all candidates for their interest; however only those selected for interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Director , eDiscovery- Technology Consulting
jobs.description:
Who We Are

FTI Consulting is the leading global expert firm for organizations facing crisis and transformation. We work with many of the world’s top multinational corporations, law firms, banks and private equity firms on their most important issues to deliver impact that makes a difference. From resolving disputes, navigating crises, managing risk and optimizing performance, our teams respond rapidly to dynamic and complex situations.

At FTI Consulting, you’ll work side-by side with leaders who have shaped history, helping solve the biggest challenges making headlines today. From day one, you’ll be an integral part of a focused team where you can make a real impact. You’ll be surrounded by an open, collaborative culture that embraces diversity, recognition, professional development and, most importantly, you.

Are you ready to make your impact?

About the Role

This Director position is within FTI Consulting's Technology practice. FTI Technology utilizes modern review platforms for native document review and case management. Our practice primarily provides professional consulting services to corporations and law firms for coordinating document review and production using Relativity and/or Nuix Discover. The Director will be responsible for managing multiple aspects of specific client matters.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who:

Is technically minded - all our work requires thinking in a logical, mathematical way about processes and sets of data
Works flexibly with a variety of team members - we work on a variety of projects at the same time, each of which can be staffed differently
Is eager and excited to learn - a positive, open-minded attitude will ensure quality work and bodes well for long-term career development
Works hard - while we do innovate, everyone has regular assigned tasks that are part of the overall workflow and on which high quality client service depends
Enjoys solving the impossible - we often receive requests that require us to consider difficult questions and develop new processes

What You'll Do

Have responsibility for day-to-day activities of projects including interaction with other consultants, supervisors, and client personnel
Apply analytical skills and leverage existing methodologies to various client situations and practice disciplines and create novel, customized solutions to meet shifting client needs
Utilize logical reasoning skills to provide complete client service
Work to ensure a quality product and delivery of all work within established timeframes.
Introduce additional FTI services to clients as needs dictate
Provide superior client service in demanding, deadline-driven situations
Maintain professional image within the firm and project same to those outside the firm

How You Will Grow

We are committed to investing and supporting you in your professional development and we have developed a range of programs focused on fostering leadership, growth and development opportunities. We aim to promote continuous learning and individual skills development through on-the-job learning, self-guided professional development courses and certifications. You’ll be assigned a dedicated coach to mentor, guide and support you through regular coaching sessions and serve as an advocate for your professional growth.

As you progress through your career at FTI Consulting, we offer tailored programs for critical professional milestones to ensure you are prepared and empowered to take on your next role.

What You Will Need To Succeed

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required
6+ relevant experience utilizing eDiscovery technology (Relativity, Nuix Discover, and/or Reveal)
Ability to travel to clients and FTI office(s) as needed
Applicants must be currently authorized to work in Canada on a full-time basis; this position does not provide visa sponsorship

Preferred Qualifications

Strong proficiency with Windows and related software, such as Microsoft Excel
Familiarity with Microsoft Access and SharePoint
Excellent communication and client interface skills
Outstanding client service in demanding, deadline–driven situations
Ability to work independently in fast-paced, multi-task environment

FTI Consulting is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, protected veteran status, religion, physical or mental disability, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, or any other basis protected by law, ordinance, or regulation.

Compensation

Minimum Pay:$125,000.00CAD

Maximum Pay:$159,500.00CAD

jobs.title: Sr. Director, Commercial Strategy & Partnerships
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Work Arrangement:
This is a hybrid position requiring candidates to work on-site at least 2 days per week at our office in Mississauga. The remaining days may be worked remotely, subject to team and business needs.

About the Role (Job Summary):

McKesson Canada is seeking a strategic and results-oriented Sr. Director, Commercial Strategy & Partnerships to lead revenue growth, new client acquisition, and strategic partnerships across our Specialty Health portfolio.

Reporting into senior leadership, you will lead a high-performing business development team responsible for expanding market share, identifying new commercial opportunities, and strengthening relationships across the healthcare ecosystem. This role combines strategic leadership, sales execution, and cross-functional collaboration to drive sustainable growth and reinforce McKesson's position as a leader in specialty healthcare solutions.

What You'll Do (Responsibilities):

Develop and execute the Specialty Health business development and sales strategy to achieve revenue growth and market expansion objectives.
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of business development professionals, establishing clear goals, performance expectations, and development plans.
Own the Specialty Health business development budget, sales forecast, and pipeline performance.
Drive new business growth by identifying, evaluating, and securing strategic partnerships and customer opportunities.
Support and coach team members in customer meetings, solution development, presentations, and negotiations.
Monitor pipeline health, sales performance, forecasting accuracy, and customer engagement metrics.
Develop business cases, financial models, and commercial proposals to support growth opportunities.
Analyze healthcare market trends, competitive intelligence, and customer insights to inform strategic decision-making.
Collaborate with Marketing, Operations, Finance, Product, and other cross-functional partners to deliver customer-focused solutions.
Build and maintain executive-level relationships with key customers, partners, and industry stakeholders.
Ensure excellence in customer interactions, proposal development, and executive presentations.
Leverage internal subject matter experts to deliver innovative solutions that drive customer and business outcomes.

Basic Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in business or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
15+ years of demonstrated success in sales and/or marketing, with a consistent track record of achieving and exceeding business objectives within the healthcare industry.
Experience within the pharmaceutical industry (brand, generic, or biosimilar) or within the Specialty space.
Proven track record of achieving and exceeding sales, revenue, and growth objectives.
Demonstrated success developing and executing strategic business development plans.
Experience managing complex sales cycles and enterprise-level customer relationships.
Exceptional communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
Experience working within matrixed organizations and leading cross-functional initiatives.
Strong executive presence with the ability to influence senior healthcare leaders and decision-makers.
Expertise in contract negotiations and strategic partnership development.

Preferred Skills/Experience:

Experience leading large, geographically dispersed, high-performing sales teams.
Strong financial acumen, including forecasting, budgeting, business case development, and ROI analysis.

The expected base salary range for this role is $190,000–$215,000, with final compensation determined based on experience, qualifications, and skills.

We are proud to offer a competitive compensation package at McKesson as part of our Total Rewards. This is determined by several factors, including performance, experience and skills, equity, regular job market evaluations, and geographical markets.
